posts.title: This implant can restore sight for patients with macular degeneration
posts.summary: More than 5 million people around the world with age-related macular degeneration (AMD) experience atrophy in their retinas. And until now, no treatment could restore their vision. The PRIMA system, which was approved in Europe in July and is awaiting FDA clearance in the US, changes that. It combines a retinal implant with camera-­equipped eyeglasses…
bullets: The PRIMA system, developed by Science Corporation, uses a retinal implant and camera-equipped glasses to restore vision in patients with advanced age-related macular degeneration (AMD).
Clinical results indicate that over 80% of recipients regained the ability to perform daily tasks like reading and using phones after training.

The technology functions by bypassing damaged photoreceptors and transmitting visual data directly to healthy retinal circuitry, powered by photovoltaic cells that eliminate the need for an internal battery.

posts.title: Roundtables: A Conversation With the Creator of AI-Designed Viruses
posts.summary: Listen to the session or watch below Can AI design new life forms? In 2025, Stanford University PhD student Samuel King came up with a preliminary answer when he used a generative AI model to propose genetic blueprints for microscopic viruses. It isn’t yet an example of AI-generated life, but that could be next. Watch…
bullets: Stanford PhD candidate Samuel King has successfully utilized generative AI models to propose genetic blueprints for microscopic viruses.
While currently limited to theoretical design, the research represents a significant intersection of generative AI and synthetic biology.
The work highlights emerging risks and capabilities in AI-driven biological design, raising questions about the future of AI-generated life forms.

posts.title: Chip Industry Week In Review
posts.summary:
Fab expansion accelerates; China advances memory and EUV; Teradyne's test deal; SEMICON West and OCP highlights; 3D SiP; TSMC and ASML signals; 300mm fab spending; optical and 3D-compute startups raise fresh funding; quantum HW advances.
The post Chip Industry Week In Review appeared first on Semiconductor Engineering.
bullets: GlobalFoundries is spearheading a $21 billion U.S.-Japan initiative to build two new fabs in Malta, New York, with operations slated to begin in 2029.
Applied Materials has launched a $5 billion EPIC Center in Silicon Valley, a 600,000-square-foot R&D facility focused on accelerating semiconductor process and equipment innovation.
ASE has introduced a 3D PowerSiP packaging solution that reduces parasitic routing losses by over 50%, significantly enhancing power efficiency for AI processors and HPC data centers.
Nvidia's share of the Chinese data-center AI-accelerator market dropped to 34% in the first half of 2026, while Huawei captured 28% of the market amid tightening export restrictions.
China's CXMT is targeting a year-end launch for DDR5 server RDIMMs using 4F² DRAM cells, a move aimed at improving memory density and reducing manufacturing costs to narrow the competitive gap.

posts.title: 2026.42: Home At Last
posts.summary: The best Stratechery content from the week of October 12, 2026, including what Apple is doing, SpaceX's appetite, and the title, takes, and the Washington Wizards.
bullets: Apple's re-entry into the home appliance market with HomeView faces skepticism regarding its strategic necessity, though proponents argue it represents a cohesive vision for the smart home ecosystem.
SpaceX is aggressively expanding its spectrum acquisition strategy, signaling a shift from providing niche emergency satellite coverage to competing for primary cellular market share.
The competitive landscape for mobile connectivity is intensifying as traditional carriers and airlines actively seek alternatives to mitigate their reliance on SpaceX's infrastructure.
The convergence of hardware, such as the new Apple TV and HomeView, suggests Apple is attempting to re-establish its influence in the living room through integrated app-based experiences.

posts.title: Shangjie Z9 electric SUV appears in regulatory filing as Huawei-SAIC brand readies fourth model
posts.summary:
The Shangjie Z9 measures 5,139 mm in length with a 3,086 mm wheelbase and offers 5-seat and 6-seat layouts.
For details, please visit CnEVPost (cnev.co).
bullets: The Shangjie Z9, a large electric SUV developed by Huawei and SAIC, has entered the MIIT regulatory filing process.
The vehicle will be offered in 5-seat and 6-seat configurations with both single-motor and dual-motor powertrain options.
The inclusion of roof-mounted LiDAR in the filing images confirms the integration of Huawei's advanced driver-assistance systems.
As the fourth model in the Shangjie lineup, the Z9 represents a significant expansion into the large SUV segment for the Huawei-led HIMA alliance.
